subject: Clarify SLA delivery profiles for streaming vs sync — contingency request
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finco.com>
To: sales@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finco.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move this to procurement review, the security and ops teams asked for clearer commitments around two delivery profiles: streaming endpoints (where their product needs near-instant first tokens) and synchronous/batch endpoints (where they rely on sustained token/sec throughput for nightly jobs).

Specific asks:
- For streaming: clear definition of Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) across 95th/99th percentiles and any carveouts during bursts.
- For streaming: guaranteed sustained token/sec per dedicated unit (and whether tokens/sec guarantees vary by model family).
- For sync/batch: max sustained tokens/sec per endpoint and latency SLO for complete response at 95p.
- Contingency language: what happens when capacity is constrained — do you automatically fall back to non-streaming variants, queue, or offer an exception?

I've attached our internal requirements spreadsheet to make it concrete (FinCo_SLA_Requirements_2026.xlsx). Procurement is asking whether Redwood can accept a written contingency that allows FinCo to invoke a temporary higher-throughput carveout for nightly reconciliation windows (2–4 hours, once per day) without penalty, provided we escalate in advance.

Could you confirm what you can commit to in writing? If you prefer, we can take a short call to walk through the attachment.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform Ops — FinCo Financial

Attachment: FinCo_SLA_Requirements_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet, 86KB)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finco.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. We'll map this to our standard SLA and flag any items that need an exception. Quick notes:

- We define TTFT as time from request accept to the first byte of model output. Our current baseline for streaming endpoints on Dedicated plans is 95p < 120ms and 99p < 250ms for common Llama-family variants at request sizes typical of conversational flows.
- Sustained token/sec guarantees are provided per dedicated GPU pool slot; they depend on model family and quantization. For example, for the M60 class (quantized), we typically guarantee 400–800 tokens/sec sustained per slot for inference-optimized models.
- For sync/batch, our 95p latency for complete responses depends heavily on max output length; we publish per-model profiles but can provide a tailored commit for fixed output bounds.

That said, the contingency you describe (scheduled nightly higher-throughput window) is a classic use case for a temporary reserved burst — we can support it, but it needs an explicit carveout in the contract (window definition, notice SLA, and any incremental usage rates).

I'll loop in Monica (security/procurement lead for these deals) and Lauren (pricing/contracting) to confirm the language and create a proposed clause. Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow to align?

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood_sla_mapping_v1.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Looping in Karthik and Lauren.

Couple of practical points before we draft a clause:
1) When we commit to per-slot sustained tokens/sec we must always include model family and typical request profile. 'Tokens/sec' without request size is ambiguous. Propose: define a standard request profile (prompt 50 tokens, response up to 150 tokens) for the guarantee, and call out conditional degradation outside that envelope.

2) For the nightly burst window, we can offer an 'elastic burst' in Dedicated where the customer pre-purchases X extra slots for a defined window at a discounted hourly rate. Alternatively, for Hosted customers we can provide prioritized routing but not absolute tokens/sec guarantees.

3) Contingency language: suggest a three-tier approach — 1) automatic fallback to compatible model variant (documented latency impact); 2) opportunistic allocation (best-effort) during constrained times; 3) customer-invoked reserved burst (requires advance notice and consumption-based pricing).

I'll draft suggested contract wording and share. Karthik — can you quick-check the numbers below for the M60 and A100 classes?

—Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Thanks — quick engineering check. Numbers below are for our current verified performance baseline (95p):
- M60 (quantized): streaming TTFT 95p <= 110ms, sustained tokens/sec 450–700 depending on model size.
- A100 (float/FP16): streaming TTFT 95p <= 85ms, sustained tokens/sec 900–1600.
- Note: sustained numbers assume continuous single-stream workload and the request profile Monica suggested (50/150). If FinCo's nightly jobs push larger context lengths or high concurrency on the same slot, throughput per-slot will drop and we need explicit extra slots.

Also: fallback behavior — we can commit to automatic fallback to an N-1 family (e.g., optimized quantized variant) with a clear delta to TTFT and sustained throughput; that fallback will be documented and included as an annex.

I'll attach a short table mapping model families to expected TTFT and tokens/sec that we can include in the clause.

—Karthik

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finco.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finco.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Thanks, Nikhil / team — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security after reviewing Monica's proposal:

- FinCo needs the carveout to be invoked with 12 hours' notice for the nightly window; billing should be consumption-only for the burst (we're not asking for committed additional seats).
- We need a written statement in the contract about automatic fallback behavior that will be used when we invoke the burst but capacity is constrained (i.e., if you cannot honor the burst, will you queue, pause lower-priority jobs, or route to a non-streaming variant).
- For compliance, we prefer a documented 99p TTFT for streaming endpoints where applicable to our highest-priority flows.

Would you be able to circulate a one-paragraph proposed contingency clause and a short appendix table with per-model TTFT/throughput ranges? If so we can route to legal.

Jane

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions — streaming TTFT and sustained token throughput

Jane — thanks for the clarifications. Attached below is the proposed contingency paragraph and the appendix we discussed. High-level summary:

- Contingency paragraph (proposed): "Customer may request a scheduled burst window (defined as a contiguous period between 1 and 4 hours, once per 24-hour period) by providing no less than 12 hours' notice. During a scheduled burst, Redwood will: (a) attempt to allocate additional Dedicated slots to satisfy the requested token/sec for the window; (b) if additional slots cannot be allocated due to system-wide capacity constraints, Redwood will (i) offer automatic fallback to a documented compatible model variant with an expected impact on TTFT and sustained throughput set out in Appendix A, or (ii) transparently notify the customer and offer to queue requests for processing once capacity frees up. Billing for the scheduled burst will be consumption-based for additional capacity consumed during the window at the rates set out in the pricing schedule."

- Appendix A: per-model family TTFT (99p) and per-slot sustained tokens/sec ranges (quantized vs FP16) — attached as CSV in this thread.

Next steps: Lauren will draft the contract addendum and send a DocuSign envelope targeted at procurement. If you'd like, we can also do a 30-minute technical readout with FinCo's ops team to confirm the Appendix baseline before legal signs off.

Thanks — Nikhil
